Classic cowboy outfit.Spurs: Spurs are worn on boot heels, and some have jingle bobs, small bells that make a distinctive sound.
Classic cowboy outfit.Chaps: Chaps come from the Spanish chaparreras, leggings meant to protect riders from thorny brush.
Classic cowboy outfit.Bandana: Cowboys wore it over their face as a dust mask, and the word comes from a Hindi word for tie-dye.
Classic cowboy outfit.Bolo tie: The bolo tie is the official neckwear of Arizona, and it was invented there in the 1940s.
Classic cowboy outfit.Cowboy boots: The high heels of cowboy boots helped keep a foot from slipping through the stirrup.
Classic cowboy outfit.Holster: It holds a pistol on the hip, and this part of the outfit was a staple of the old West and its movies.
Classic cowboy outfit.Duster coat: Long coats called dusters shielded riders from trail dust, and their name is exactly their job.
Classic cowboy outfit.Leather vest: A leather vest protects the torso while keeping arms free for roping, and fits the outfit.
Classic cowboy outfit.Ten-gallon hat: The name may not refer to volume at all, possibly from Spanish galon, braid, since the hat holds about a gallon at most.
Classic cowboy outfit.Kilt: The kilt is Scottish, a pleated tartan wrap that has nothing to do with the American West.
Classic cowboy outfit.Turban: The turban is worn across South Asia and the Middle East, and in Sikhism it is a religious article.
Classic cowboy outfit.Toga: The toga is an ancient Roman garment draped from a long piece of wool.
Classic cowboy outfit.Tutu: Tutus are for ballet, and the stiff version dates to the Romantic era.
Classic cowboy outfit.Beret: Berets are classic in France and the Basque region, the opposite of a cowboy hat.
Classic cowboy outfit.Kimono: The kimono, meaning thing to wear, is Japanese, long robes tied with an obi.
Classic cowboy outfit.Sari: A sari is a single length of cloth, up to nine yards long, wrapped and draped in South Asia.
Classic cowboy outfit.Monocle: The monocle is a single eyeglass lens, which a gentleman wore, not a cowboy.
Classic cowboy outfit.Lederhosen: Lederhosen are Bavarian leather shorts, the opposite of rugged cowboy chaps.
Classic cowboy outfit.Top hat: The top hat was a city gentleman's piece, so it is not a classic cowboy piece.
Classic cowboy outfit.Clogs: Clogs are Dutch wooden shoes, designed for wet fields.
Classic cowboy outfit.Sarong: The sarong is a wrapped skirt from Southeast Asia, not typical for a cowboy.
Classic cowboy outfit.Fez: The fez is named after the Moroccan city of Fez, and was Ottoman fashion in the 1800s.
Classic cowboy outfit.Tiara: A tiara is a royal jeweled crown, the opposite of a rugged cowboy.

Parts of a wristwatch.Crown: The crown is the small knob for setting time and winding; on dive watches it screws down to keep out water.
Parts of a wristwatch.Bezel: The bezel is the ring around the dial; on dive watches it rotates to time how long you've been underwater.
Parts of a wristwatch.Dial: The dial is the watch's face, and collectors prize rare dials; patina on old ones can raise prices.
Parts of a wristwatch.Hands: Watch hands are often shaped as Breguet or sword style; Hollywood often sets them at 10:10 for a smile effect in ads.
Parts of a wristwatch.Strap: The strap can be leather, metal or rubber; swapping it is the cheapest way to change a watch's look.
Parts of a wristwatch.Crystal: Crystal is the clear cover on the dial; sapphire crystal is nearly as hard as diamond and resists scratches.
Parts of a wristwatch.Lug: Lugs are the horns that hold the strap pins, and lug-to-lug width decides whether a watch fits your wrist.
Parts of a wristwatch.Movement: The movement is the watch's engine, either mechanical or quartz; a mechanical one has well over 100 tiny parts.
Parts of a wristwatch.Mainspring: The mainspring is a coiled ribbon of steel that stores energy; when it unwinds, it powers the watch.
Parts of a wristwatch.Escapement: The escapement releases power in tiny, even steps, creating the tick; it is the heart of a mechanical watch.
Parts of a wristwatch.Balance wheel: The balance wheel swings back and forth many times a second, regulating the movement like a tiny pendulum.
Parts of a wristwatch.Lapel: A lapel is the folded part of a jacket collar, and the notched one is cut near the buttonhole; nothing to do with watches.
Parts of a wristwatch.Aglet: An aglet is the plastic or metal tip of a shoelace, so it belongs to shoes and not watches.
Parts of a wristwatch.Eyelet: An eyelet is a small hole for a lace or cord, not part of a watch.
Parts of a wristwatch.Pendulum: A pendulum regulates grandfather clocks, not wristwatches; Galileo studied it and Huygens built the first pendulum clock in 1656.
Parts of a wristwatch.Cuckoo: A cuckoo is a clock bird, but wristwatches don't have one; cuckoo clocks come from Germany's Black Forest.
Parts of a wristwatch.Brim: A brim is a hat's edge and not a watch part.
Parts of a wristwatch.Hem: A hem is a folded edge of cloth, and isn't on a watch.
Parts of a wristwatch.Sole: A sole is the underside of a shoe, with nothing to do with watches.
Parts of a wristwatch.Heel: A heel is the back of a shoe or foot, not a watch part.
Parts of a wristwatch.Placket: A placket is the fabric strip with buttons on a shirt, not on a watch.
Parts of a wristwatch.Tassel: A tassel is a decorative tuft of threads, and so not part of a watch.
Parts of a wristwatch.Pleat: A pleat is a fold sewn into fabric, so not a watch part.
Parts of a wristwatch.Shoelace: A shoelace is no watch part; its plastic tip, the aglet, shares a name with nothing on a dial, though both are small precision pieces.
